pairs.questionText: Why does ice float on water? Explain in terms of density.
pairs.answerText: Ice floats on water because ice is less dense than liquid water - the hexagonal crystal structure formed on freezing takes up more space than the liquid.

pairs.questionText: Specific heat and heating of water. Define specific heat capacity.
pairs.answerText:
Q8(a)
Specific heat capacity is the heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a
substance by 1 degree Celsius.

pairs.questionText: Calculate the heat required to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water from 20 degrees Celsius to 80 degrees Celsius. (Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kg-degC)
pairs.answerText:
Q8(b)
Q = m c (delta)T = 2 x 4200 x 60 = 504000 J
